attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, given as his own assertion.

semantics.note: The draft keeps all three clauses: revenue growth, business value and losses on adopted products. Rewording 'grotesque loss' as 'large losses' is acceptable. This is a present-tense description of the industry.

contract.note: Using Q1 2025 as the period and reading 'significant' as commercially meaningful are fair, ordinary readings. Still, the result depends on unstated choices: which products count, the accounting basis, and whether the claim is universal or a generalisation.

evidence.note: Klarna's own disclosure of a 22% cut in service cost per transaction in Q1 2025. It speaks only to one customer's business value. It is not independent, leaves implementation and quality costs out, and says nothing about supplier revenue or losses.
Report from May 2025 on the CEO's concerns that AI service quality was lower and on renewed human hiring. It qualifies the Klarna savings but does not measure any clause for the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no product-level revenue or profitability data for generative AI suppliers in Q1 2025. The only business-value evidence is one company's self-reported savings, which its own CEO's quality concerns undercut. None of the three clauses is settled either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own recap point in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The draft keeps both companies, the 'billions a year after revenue' loss and the 'stories' comparison as written.

contract.note: Reading 'billions' as at least $2B each, using 2024 as the year and taking net loss on an estimate basis are fair, ordinary readings. The comparison of 'stories' has no stated test and cannot be scored.

evidence.note: Reuters, on an estimate basis, reports that OpenAI lost about $5B in 2024. This supports the OpenAI part only.

Anthropic's S-1, published before the cutoff, shows an audited GAAP 2024 net loss of $8.3B, of which $5.4B is fair-value changes. GAAP is a different accounting basis from the contract's estimate basis, so this is context only.

reviews.rationale: The OpenAI loss clause is supported on the contract's basis. Anthropic's 2024 loss appears only on a GAAP basis that differs from the contract, so that part is not established as specified. The comparison of 'stories' has no test. Nothing is contradicted, but the compound claim is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, introducing his section on Cursor.

semantics.note: An unhedged claim that only one route works, about where generative AI can make money. Here 'can' expresses a firm structural claim, not a hedge.

contract.note: Reading 'make money' as substantial profit fits the passage's focus on profitability, but the speaker did not say it. A revenue reading could favour counterexamples such as advertising. Tying an ongoing claim to Q2 2025 is also an inference.

evidence.note: Google's own announcement that it is expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode. It shows a non-subscription way to earn money but gives no profit figure.

Reports Google's claim that AI Overviews monetise at the same rate as ordinary search. That is a relative revenue measure the company reported itself, with no costs or profit, so it does not meet the contract's profit test.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows advertising revenue from generative AI outside SaaS but does not establish that it is profitable. It also cannot show that profits were confined to SaaS. Neither condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own closing statement in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The unhedged 'will harm' is a forecast. 'Needless, wasteful' and 'must be held accountable' are normative and are rightly left out. The draft keeps all three areas of harm.

contract.note: Requiring material harm in markets, the wider economy and the tech industry is a fair plain reading. The forecast has no deadline, and the size and geography of the harm are unspecified. The 'retrospective' label is odd for a forecast but does not change the result.

evidence.note: KOSPI's sharp tech selloff in July 2026, linked to doubts about returns on AI spending. This bears on the markets part only. It is a non-US market and shows no wider economic harm.
The IMF says markets have stayed resilient and describes an AI-driven correction only as a risk scenario. It does not establish that the forecast harm has happened.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline. The early-resolution rule needs AI-attributable harm in all three areas, and the evidence shows only a regional market selloff. The IMF reports resilience, with AI harm still only a risk. The forecast cannot be scored yet.
